name: Paul Erdős
milestone_by_age_26: Published an elegant elementary proof of Bertrand's postulate (Chebyshev's theorem) at age 18 in 1932, earned his PhD at 21 in 1934, and co-authored the seminal Happy Ending problem paper with George Szekeres in 1935, among numerous early publications in number theory and combinatorics.
early_history_summary: Both of Erdős's parents were mathematics teachers who introduced him to mathematics early. He was homeschooled with tutors due to his mother's overprotectiveness after losing two daughters. He won a national examination to enter university in 1930 despite anti-Jewish restrictions, published his first paper at 16, and completed his doctorate at 21.
family_context_summary: Born to a well-to-do Hungarian-Jewish family; both parents were high school mathematics teachers. His father was captured and held in Siberia during WWI for six years, and his mother was dismissed from her teaching post due to political circumstances.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were mathematics teachers who directly introduced Erdős to mathematics. His father taught him English during captivity and his mother provided early mathematical instruction.
primary_early_advantage_tags: math teacher parents, homeschooling, national examination winner, early publications, Jewish restrictions
evidence_summary: Erdős published his first mathematical paper at 16 and produced an elementary proof of Bertrand's postulate at 18, a result that had stood since 1850. Both parents were mathematics teachers who provided direct domain instruction. He won a national examination to enter university despite anti-Jewish laws, earned his PhD at 21, and co-authored the seminal Happy Ending problem paper at 22. His prolific early output was driven by deep mathematical talent nurtured by family-domain apprenticeship and intense concentration.

name: Edsger Dijkstra
milestone_by_age_26: Invented Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm in 1956 at age 26 while at the Mathematical Centre in Amsterdam, a foundational algorithm in computer science still used universally in routing, networking, and pathfinding applications today.
early_history_summary: Dijkstra studied theoretical physics at the University of Leyden and began programming part-time at the Mathematical Centre in Amsterdam in 1952 after his father spotted a Cambridge programming course advertisement. He became one of the Netherlands' first programmers, working under Aad van Wijngaarden, and developed the shortest path algorithm for the ARMAC computer's public inauguration in 1956.
family_context_summary: Father was a high school chemistry teacher in Rotterdam; mother was trained as a mathematician though she never held a formal position. His father subscribed to Nature and spotted the Cambridge programming course advertisement that launched Dijkstra's computing career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was trained as a mathematician with great agility in manipulating formulae and elegant problem-solving, providing early mathematical influence. Father was a chemistry teacher who facilitated the pivotal Cambridge programming course.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mathematician mother, Cambridge programming course, Mathematical Centre Amsterdam, early computing access, van Wijngaarden mentorship
evidence_summary: Dijkstra developed the shortest path algorithm in 1956 at age 26 for the ARMAC computer demonstration at the Mathematical Centre in Amsterdam, where he had been programming since 1952. His mother was a trained mathematician and his father, a chemistry teacher, spotted the Cambridge programming course that launched his computing career. He was one of the first programmers in the Netherlands with access to rare early computing hardware, mentored by Aad van Wijngaarden at the Mathematical Centre.

name: Janus Friis
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded KaZaA in 2000-2001 at age 24, which became the world's most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing application after Napster's shutdown, with hundreds of millions of downloads globally by age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Friis dropped out of high school and taught himself computer skills while working at the help desk of CyberCity, one of Denmark's first ISPs. He met Niklas Zennström at Tele2 in 1996, collaborated on ISP ventures, then moved to Amsterdam in January 2000 to develop KaZaA with Zennström, launching it in March 2001.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Friis had no formal higher education, dropping out of high school.
primary_early_advantage_tags: high school dropout, self-taught, ISP help desk, Zennström partnership, P2P wave, Tele2
evidence_summary: Friis co-founded KaZaA at age 24, which became the world's most popular file-sharing application after Napster's shutdown, with hundreds of millions of downloads. He had no formal education beyond high school but taught himself computing at an early ISP help desk. His partnership with Niklas Zennström was the critical complementary team factor, and they rode the massive P2P file-sharing structural wave. His early ISP work provided direct domain exposure to internet infrastructure.

name: John Romero
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991 at age 23, shipped the seminal Commander Keen series (December 1990), Wolfenstein 3D (May 1992), and Doom (December 1993) by age 26, games that defined and popularized the first-person shooter genre.
early_history_summary: Romero began programming at age 11 on an Apple II Plus, self-taught, and had created over 70 games by his first professional job at Origin Systems in 1987 at age 20. He worked at Softdisk starting in 1989, where he hired John Carmack and partnered with Tom Hall and Adrian Carmack to create Commander Keen in their spare time, leading to the founding of id Software in February 1991.
family_context_summary: Born to Ginny and Alfonso Antonio Romero, a maintenance man at an air force base. The family had Mexican, Yaqui, and Cherokee heritage. Grew up in difficult circumstances including exposure to drugs and violence. His stepfather later moved the family to an RAF base in England.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in technology or gaming. Father was a maintenance man; no domain expertise transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught programmer, 70+ games by age 20, Apple II, Carmack partnership, shareware distribution, PC gaming wave
evidence_summary: Romero co-founded id Software at 23 and shipped Commander Keen, Wolfenstein 3D, and Doom by age 26, defining the FPS genre. He was entirely self-taught, creating over 70 games before his first professional job at 20. His partnership with John Carmack was the critical complementary team factor—Romero handled design and tools while Carmack drove engine technology. He rode the PC gaming and shareware distribution wave, with intense concentration on game development from childhood despite a difficult family background with no tech domain advantage.

name: Erwin Schrödinger
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Schrödinger earned his doctorate in 1910 at age 23 and his habilitation in 1914 at age 27, but his first important paper was published in 1914 (age 27) and the Schrödinger equation was formulated in 1926 at age 39. No seminal publication or major discovery by age 26 (August 1913) was found.
early_history_summary: Schrödinger studied at the University of Vienna under Fritz Hasenöhrl, earning his doctorate in 1910 at age 23. He worked as an assistant in experimental physics under Franz Exner and completed his habilitation in 1914. His early work focused on dielectric properties, atmospheric electricity, and radioactivity before his landmark wave mechanics work in 1926.
family_context_summary: Son of a textile manufacturer and hobby botanist. Grew up in Vienna in a cultured household where both English and German were spoken. Received private tutoring at home until age 10.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a textile manufacturer and hobby botanist; no direct physics domain transfer documented, though the family valued intellectual pursuits.
